text:
Alternating homogeneous task batches changes optimization beyond supervision alone. Adam maintains moving averages of gradients and squared gradients; separate terminal/reconstruction steps update these statistics sequentially, with the second gradient evaluated at changed parameters. Consequently, alternating updates generally differ from applying Adam once to a weighted mixed-task gradient—even with equal task exposure. This follows from [Adam’s update equations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6980). Empirically, [Gottumukkala et al.](https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.86/) found mixed-task batches beneficial over homogeneous batches in reading comprehension; transfer to BERT4Rec remains unverified.

Normalization defines the intended objective. For explicit task weighting, use L = λ·S_terminal/N_terminal + (1−λ)·S_mask/N_mask, where S sums supervised-position losses and N counts actual targets, excluding padding and ignored positions. Pooling both sums over N_terminal+N_mask instead weights tasks by target counts: reconstruction receives more weight when it supplies more masked positions. Averaging per-batch or per-sequence means introduces another weighting when counts differ. [Hugging Face’s documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/grad_accumulation) explains why accumulated token means require the total supervised-token denominator.

A focused control would compare alternating and mixed batching while matching task exposure, target counts, explicit loss weights, optimizer-step count, learning-rate schedule and clipping placement; report compute separately. Accumulating both task gradients at unchanged parameters before one Adam step isolates homogeneous microbatch execution from sequential optimizer updates and reproduces the weighted combined gradient, subject to stochastic/numerical differences. Keep this as a targeted diagnostic rather than expanding the main search; log each task’s target counts, mean loss and occasional gradient norms. In bidirectional BERT4Rec, keep the terminal prediction target hidden.
